clue: A chronological record of who accessed a system, what they changed, and when.
description: A log of user actions inside a system, with the time each one happened.
why: It lets auditors trace any change back to a person; if users can edit it, nothing in it can be trusted.

clue: The test of whether an error is large enough to change the decision of someone relying on reports.
description: Materiality is the threshold above which a misstatement matters to the people who use the reports.
why: It tells auditors what to report and where to focus, so they do not drown in one-peso differences.

clue: Logs, screenshots, interview notes and re-performed calculations an auditor gathers to support an opinion.
description: The information an auditor collects to back up each finding; it must be sufficient, relevant and reliable.
why: An audit opinion is only as strong as the proof behind it.

clue: Testing a selected subset of transactions and projecting the results to the whole population.
description: Checking some items instead of all of them, then drawing a conclusion about the full set.
why: No team can test every transaction, so this is how audits stay possible within time and budget.

clue: The chance a material error happens before any safeguards are applied to a system.
description: The level of risk built into an activity itself, such as large automatic money transfers.
why: It tells auditors which systems deserve the closest look before they even test any controls.

clue: The chance that an organization's own safeguards fail to prevent or catch an error.
description: The risk that internal controls do not work as designed.
why: High values here mean the auditor must test more transactions directly instead of trusting the controls.

clue: A framework for the governance and management of enterprise IT, used to map controls.
description: COBIT is a widely used framework of IT governance objectives, processes and maturity levels.
why: It gives auditors and management a shared language, so findings map to recognized objectives.

clue: The global professional association that issues the CISA certification and publishes audit guidance.
description: ISACA is the professional body for IT audit, governance and security practitioners.
why: Its standards and the CISA credential define how IT audits are done in the Philippines and worldwide.

clue: Freedom from relationships that could bias an auditor's judgment about the systems reviewed.
description: Being free of conflicts of interest, so a programmer never audits the system they built.
why: Without it, management and regulators cannot rely on any audit finding.

clue: Confidence given to management and the board that systems are reliable and assets are safe.
description: The level of confidence an audit provides about systems, data and assets.
why: It is the product an audit delivers: decision makers act on it.
